questions.question_text:
A project engineer has a taxable income of $\$132\,900$.
$\begin{array}{l|l} \textbf{Taxable income} & \textbf{Tax on this income} \\ \hline \$0\text{ to }\$18\,200 & \text{Nil} \\ \$18\,201\text{ to }\$45\,000 & 19\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$18\,200 \\ \$45\,001\text{ to }\$120\,000 & \$5092\text{ plus }32.5\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$45\,000 \\ \$120\,001\text{ to }\$180\,000 & \$29\,467\text{ plus }37\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$120\,000 \\ \$180\,001\text{ and over} & \$51\,667\text{ plus }45\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$180\,000 \end{array}$
Which tax bracket does her taxable income fall into?

options.why: Chose the row whose upper limit ($\$120\,000$) is just below the income instead of the row that contains it.
Counted the heading row as the first bracket, shifting every bracket number down by one.
Counted the rows from the bottom of the table upwards instead of from the top.

questions.solution_text:
$\$132\,900$ is more than $\$120\,000$ and not more than $\$180\,000$.
It lies in the fourth bracket.

questions.question_text:
A student nurse has a taxable income of $\$17\,900$.
$\begin{array}{l|l} \textbf{Taxable income} & \textbf{Tax on this income} \\ \hline \$0\text{ to }\$18\,200 & \text{Nil} \\ \$18\,201\text{ to }\$45\,000 & 19\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$18\,200 \\ \$45\,001\text{ to }\$120\,000 & \$5092\text{ plus }32.5\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$45\,000 \\ \$120\,001\text{ to }\$180\,000 & \$29\,467\text{ plus }37\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$120\,000 \\ \$180\,001\text{ and over} & \$51\,667\text{ plus }45\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$180\,000 \end{array}$
What is her income tax payable, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Applied the second bracket’s $19$c rate to the whole income, ignoring that $\$17\,900$ is below $\$18\,200$.
Found the amount the income falls short of $\$18\,200$ and taxed that $\$300$ at $19$c.
Taxed the threshold $\$18\,200$ at $19$c instead of recognising the first bracket is nil.

questions.solution_text:
$\$17\,900$ lies in the first bracket ($\$0\text{ to }\$18\,200$), which is taxed at nil.
$\text{Tax payable}=\$0.00$

questions.question_text:
A laboratory technician at an engineering firm has a taxable income of $\$28\,400$.
$\begin{array}{l|l} \textbf{Taxable income} & \textbf{Tax on this income} \\ \hline \$0\text{ to }\$18\,200 & \text{Nil} \\ \$18\,201\text{ to }\$45\,000 & 19\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$18\,200 \\ \$45\,001\text{ to }\$120\,000 & \$5092\text{ plus }32.5\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$45\,000 \\ \$120\,001\text{ to }\$180\,000 & \$29\,467\text{ plus }37\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$120\,000 \\ \$180\,001\text{ and over} & \$51\,667\text{ plus }45\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$180\,000 \end{array}$
What is his income tax payable, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Applied $19$c to the whole taxable income instead of only to the excess over $\$18\,200$.
Used the third bracket’s $32.5$c rate on the correct excess of $\$10\,200$.
Added the third bracket’s base tax of $\$5092$, although the second bracket has no base tax.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Determine the tax bracket**
$\$28\,400$ lies in the second bracket ($\$18\,201\text{ to }\$45\,000$).
2. **Calculate the excess**
$\text{Excess}=28\,400-18\,200$
$=\$10\,200$
3. **Calculate the tax payable**
$\text{Tax payable}=0+0.19\times10\,200$
$=\$1938.00$

questions.question_text:
A clinical nurse consultant has a taxable income of $\$92\,000$.
$\begin{array}{l|l} \textbf{Taxable income} & \textbf{Tax on this income} \\ \hline \$0\text{ to }\$18\,200 & \text{Nil} \\ \$18\,201\text{ to }\$45\,000 & 19\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$18\,200 \\ \$45\,001\text{ to }\$120\,000 & \$5092\text{ plus }32.5\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$45\,000 \\ \$120\,001\text{ to }\$180\,000 & \$29\,467\text{ plus }37\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$120\,000 \\ \$180\,001\text{ and over} & \$51\,667\text{ plus }45\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$180\,000 \end{array}$
What is her income tax payable, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Applied $32.5$c to the whole taxable income instead of only to the excess over $\$45\,000$.
Left out the base tax of $\$5092$ and gave only the tax on the excess.
Measured the excess from $\$18\,200$ instead of from $\$45\,000$.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Determine the tax bracket**
$\$92\,000$ lies in the third bracket ($\$45\,001\text{ to }\$120\,000$).
2. **Calculate the excess**
$\text{Excess}=92\,000-45\,000$
$=\$47\,000$
3. **Calculate the tax payable**
$\text{Tax payable}=5092+0.325\times47\,000$
$=\$20\,367.00$

questions.question_text:
The table shows the personal income tax rates for a different country.
The base tax of a bracket is the total tax payable on all the income in the brackets below it.
$\begin{array}{l|l} \textbf{Taxable income} & \textbf{Tax on this income} \\ \hline \$0\text{ to }\$24\,000 & \text{Nil} \\ \$24\,001\text{ to }\$65\,000 & 24\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$24\,000 \\ \$65\,001\text{ and over} & \$a\text{ plus }39\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$65\,000 \end{array}$
What is the value of $a$, to the nearest dollar?

options.why: Taxed the whole $\$65\,000$ at $24$c instead of only the part above $\$24\,000$.
Taxed the tax-free amount $\$24\,000$ at $24$c instead of the band above it.
Applied the top bracket’s $39$c rate to the whole $\$65\,000$ instead of applying $24$c only to the income above $\$24\,000$.

questions.solution_text:
$a$ is the total tax payable on a taxable income of $\$65\,000$, which lies in the second bracket.
$a=0.24\times(65\,000-24\,000)$
$=0.24\times41\,000$
$=\$9840$
